Hi Asha / Markus —

Thanks again for the productive demo last week. As discussed, you asked for a committed Reserved Pool for your 32k-context model workload and clarity on how quantization choices affect GPU count and pricing. I attached a working capacity workbook (Lumina_capacity_model_v3.xlsx) and a first-pass SOW.

Quick summary upfront:
- We scoped two configuration ladders: conservative (FP16 model weights + KV hot-cache) and aggressive (4-bit quantization + offload-friendly KV).
- Conservative = higher per-GPU memory requirement, fewer model variants to manage; Aggressive = lower memory per GPU but requires a small engineering validation window (~2 weeks) and slightly higher tail latency risk for long-tail sessions.

Requested next steps:
1) Can you confirm expected concurrency (avg sessions / peak sessions) for the inference endpoint? We used 75 concurrent sessions peak in the attached workbook as a placeholder.
2) Are regulatory constraints (data residency / HSM) in play for the pilot?

I'll loop in our infra lead Jonas and product ops Marissa to lock down sizing and committed headroom. Goal: deliver a 6-12 month reserved capacity quote with an explicit "memory surge buffer" for long-context sessions.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Evelyn / Marissa —

I ran an initial sizing pass against the model profile you shared (70B-class architecture, 64 layers, 32k tokens target). Below are the pragmatic numbers we should present to Lumina; I'll keep commentary brief and put full math in the attachment of the workbook.

Assumptions:
- Baseline FP16 model weights roughly 70GB memory footprint in GPU memory (includes some host staging).
- 4-bit quantized (dynamic 4-bit) reduces weight approx 2.8x -> ~25GB resident (material depends on quant backend).
- KV cache: at our runtime a conservative estimate is ~0.6MB per token for this model family (all layers aggregated, keys+values).
- For 32k context that implies ~19GB KV cache per active session (32,000 * 0.6KB = ~19,200KB? see note below).

Sizing table (per-GPU capacity needed to serve single replica with single-streamed KV):
- FP16 ladder (no quant): model weights 70GB + KV 19GB + runtime headroom 6GB -> ~95GB.
- 4-bit ladder: model weights 25GB + KV 19GB + runtime headroom 6GB -> ~50GB.

Operational notes:
- That KV estimate is intentionally conservative; our optimized KV packing can reduce to ~0.35MB/token in practice for some attention variants, which lowers KV to ~11GB for 32k. We'll propose two KV profiles in the workbook (conservative / optimized).
- For reserved-pool planning: recommend sizing GPUs as follows:
  * Conservative offer (FP16 + conservative KV): 4x A100-80GB equivalents per serving cluster node (we price per-GPU). For expected peak concurrency 120 sessions and aiming for p50 latency SLO we need 18 replicas (math in spreadsheet) -> recommend 18 GPUs reserved + 4 GPUs surge = 22 GPUs committed.
  * Aggressive offer (4-bit + optimized KV): 1x A100-80GB equivalent per replica fits ~2-3 concurrent sessions per GPU depending on batching. For 120 peak sessions we recommend 10 GPUs reserved + 3 surge = 13 GPUs committed.

Trade-offs to call out for the customer deck:
- Aggressive ladder reduces committed GPU count by ~40–50% but requires extra validation (quality delta), and smaller headroom for unexpected long-tail sessions.
- We should include a 20% "memory surge buffer" on any committed pool to avoid immediate falls to fallback models during peaks.

I'll attach my sizing sheet into the workbook tab "InfraSizing_JW". If Lumina wants strict isolation we can propose dedicated machines sized to the conservative bucket and a separate burst pool for the aggressive lane.

-Jonas
Senior Infra Architect, Redwood Inference

Asha / Markus —

Quick reply with plan and next milestones:

1) Pricing / per-token delta:
- Conservative (FP16): estimated committed monthly = $38,400/mo for 22-GPU reserved pool (includes 20% memory surge buffer). Estimated per-inference token cost (avg) = $0.00038/token (workbook has full monthly burn scenarios).
- Aggressive (4-bit): estimated committed monthly = $24,700/mo for 13-GPU reserved pool. Estimated per-token = $0.00022/token.

2) Failover automation: Redwood supports policy-based routing at the request level — we can configure an automatic fallback policy: if quality score falls below configured threshold for X% of requests over a rolling window, route new requests to the FP16 variant or to a higher-memory pool. This is part of our rollouts feature and doesn't require extra infra engineering (ops time to configure + runbook).

3) 2-week validation: we include a one-week staging validation and a one-week AB-run where you send representative prompts. That effort is included as a pilot line item (no extra markup) in the attached SOW; if deeper model retuning is required we'll scope separately.

Next milestone: we'll turn this into a formal SOW and an initial reserved quote. Can you confirm procurement/legal contact for contract redlines?

Best,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
